text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Parliament speaker Berri who met French President Chirac in Paris said Chirac believes that it is in the interests of both Syria and Lebanon to remain togather until peace is achieved in the region.
-Balance of payments registered a $24 million surplus in February for a cumulative surplus of $227 million in the first two months of 1997.
-Weekly treasury bill issue of March 20 raised 366 billion Lebanese pounds and posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 122 billion pounds.
-Yields were mixed on Lebanese treasury bills with the three and six months t-bills falling and 12 and 24 months t-bills remaining steady.
-Foreign Minister Bouez headed to Morocco for a meeting of Jerusalem Committee to be held on Saturday.
-Israeli shelling on suspected Hizbollah (Party of God) positions in South Lebanon.
-The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks rose, in dollar terms, to $24,085 million in January from $23,993 million in December 1996, the Lebanese Banks Association said.
-Three members of a radical Moslem group were executed by hanging more than two months after they were sentenced to death for killing a rival Islamist cleric in 1995.
- Teachers at state-owned Lebanese University will go on one-day strike on April 3 to protest at latest government's academic decisions.
-Workers of public utilitities will go on open-ended strike on April 3 to pressure the government for pay demands.
